note: Scripted streams for PASK's LatentNeeds-Bench protocol. Each stream is one long conversation, already transcribed and attributed to speakers (the format bench/03b_rewrite.py produces), split into an earlier part and a later part the way bench/02_build_turns.py splits sessions into parts. The memory writer (bench/03c_memory.py) reads the earlier part at the part boundary; demand detection (eval/prompts.py) runs on every turn of the later part. 'need_turns' (0-based, later part) marks where something said only in the earlier part makes a need detectable; 'cues' are case-insensitive regular expressions for facts stated only in the earlier part (not in the scene or the later part); 'design' says why the stream was chosen. need_turns, cues and design are for analysis only and are never sent to a model.

streams.design: work meeting; a compliance constraint stated before a break is contradicted when the plan is locked after it

scene.scene: A product team's launch-planning meeting for version 3.0 of a note-taking app. The meeting resumes after a ten-minute break.

characters.name: Alex Chen
characters.background: owns the 3.0 launch plan and its sign-off

characters.name: Priya Nair
characters.background: covers legal questions for the product team

characters.name: Marco Rossi
characters.background: runs the launch campaign and customer emails

primary_user.name: Alex Chen
primary_user.reason: as product manager he has to lock the launch plan before the meeting ends

earlier.speaker: Alex Chen
earlier.text: Okay, first item is the 3.0 launch. Marco, where is the campaign?

earlier.speaker: Marco Rossi
earlier.text: Assets are done. We're targeting October 14 for both the US and the EU, and the press embargo lifts that morning.

earlier.speaker: Jin Park
earlier.text: Engineering is on track. Voice Notes, the new recording feature, is code-complete and passed QA last night.

earlier.speaker: Priya Nair
earlier.text: One flag from me. Voice Notes records other people in meetings, so in the EU it can't go live until our DPIA is signed off.

earlier.speaker: Alex Chen
earlier.text: When do you expect the sign-off?

earlier.speaker: Priya Nair
earlier.text: The external reviewer says October 21 at the earliest. Until then Voice Notes has to stay off for EU accounts.

earlier.speaker: Marco Rossi
earlier.text: Noted. Let's take ten minutes and then do the pricing page.

later.speaker: Marco Rossi
later.text: Pricing page is final: three tiers, and the annual plan gets two months free.

later.speaker: Jin Park
later.text: Also, every 3.0 feature sits behind a feature flag, and flags can be set per region in the admin console.

later.speaker: Alex Chen
later.text: Great. Then let's lock it: on October 14 we go live in the US and the EU with the full 3.0 feature set, Voice Notes included.

later.speaker: Marco Rossi
later.text: Perfect. I'll schedule the launch emails for 8 a.m. local time in each region.

streams.design: learning session; the data structure explained early (repeated measures) makes the planned test invalid later

scene.scene: An online tutoring session in which a master's student plans the analysis of her thesis study with a statistics tutor.

characters.name: Sofia Alvarez
characters.background: kinesiology student writing her thesis on a stretching program

characters.name: Ben Okafor
characters.background: helps graduate students with study design and analysis

primary_user.name: Sofia Alvarez
primary_user.reason: she decides how to analyse her thesis data and will report the result

earlier.speaker: Ben Okafor
earlier.text: Before we pick a test, walk me through how the data were collected.

earlier.speaker: Sofia Alvarez
earlier.text: Forty participants, twenty in the stretching group and twenty controls. Each person did the balance test three times, at week 0, 4 and 8.

earlier.speaker: Ben Okafor
earlier.text: So every participant gives you three scores, and the scores from one person are correlated. They are not independent observations.

earlier.speaker: Sofia Alvarez
earlier.text: Right, the same person tends to score about the same each time.

earlier.speaker: Ben Okafor
earlier.text: Exactly. Keep that in mind. Students often treat repeated scores as separate people, and their p-values come out far too small.

earlier.speaker: Sofia Alvarez
earlier.text: Got it. Can we look at my figures for a bit? My advisor hated the colors.

later.speaker: Ben Okafor
later.text: These plots look much better with the colorblind-safe palette.

later.speaker: Sofia Alvarez
later.text: Thanks! For the main result I put everything in one sheet: 120 rows, one per balance score, with a column for the group.

later.speaker: Sofia Alvarez
later.text: So I'll run an independent-samples t-test on all 120 scores, stretching versus control, and report that as my main finding.

later.speaker: Ben Okafor
later.text: Let's also make sure the write-up says which software and version you used.

streams.design: daily life; a guest's allergy mentioned in the afternoon matters when dinner is ordered in the evening

scene.scene: Three friends spend a Saturday together and in the evening order dinner for the group, which now includes a fourth guest.

characters.name: Jordan Lee
characters.background: is organising and paying for tonight's dinner

characters.name: Mia Torres
characters.background: her partner is joining the group for dinner

characters.name: Kai Brooks
characters.background: a regular at the local restaurants

primary_user.name: Jordan Lee
primary_user.reason: he is ordering dinner for everyone tonight

earlier.speaker: Mia Torres
earlier.text: Sam's coming tonight after his shift. He's excited to finally meet everyone.

earlier.speaker: Jordan Lee
earlier.text: Great, then I'll order dinner for four.

earlier.speaker: Mia Torres
earlier.text: Just so you know, Sam has a severe peanut allergy. Even food cooked in the same pan can set it off, and he carries an EpiPen.

earlier.speaker: Jordan Lee
earlier.text: Good to know, thanks.

earlier.speaker: Kai Brooks
earlier.text: Did anyone see the match last night? That last-minute goal was unreal.

earlier.speaker: Mia Torres
earlier.text: I missed it, we were at his sister's birthday.

later.speaker: Kai Brooks
later.text: I'm starving. Can we order already?

later.speaker: Jordan Lee
later.text: Yeah, the Thai place on Elm Street delivers in about thirty minutes.

later.speaker: Jordan Lee
later.text: Let's get the chicken satay platter with extra peanut sauce, a big pad thai and a green curry for everyone to share.

later.speaker: Kai Brooks
later.text: Add the spring rolls too, they're great there.

streams.design: technical planning; a maintenance window announced early conflicts with the time chosen later

scene.scene: An engineering team's planning call for a schema change on the orders service.

characters.name: Lena Fischer
characters.background: owns the orders service and schedules its migrations

primary_user.name: Lena Fischer
primary_user.reason: she decides when the migration runs

earlier.speaker: Lena Fischer
earlier.text: Quick round of updates before we plan the orders migration.

earlier.speaker: Omar Haddad
earlier.text: Heads-up: the provider moved our orders database maintenance. It's now this Thursday, 02:00 to 04:00 UTC, and the primary fails over during it.

earlier.speaker: Tom Becker
earlier.text: During failover, writes pause for a few minutes and any long-running schema change gets killed.

earlier.speaker: Omar Haddad
earlier.text: So nothing heavy on the orders database in that window, please.

earlier.speaker: Lena Fischer
earlier.text: Understood. Tom, anything else from on-call?

earlier.speaker: Tom Becker
earlier.text: Just the usual noisy disk alerts on the analytics boxes. I'm tuning them.

later.speaker: Lena Fischer
later.text: Okay, the migration itself: we add the delivery_window column and backfill it.

later.speaker: Omar Haddad
later.text: The backfill touches about forty million rows, so expect around ninety minutes.

later.speaker: Lena Fischer
later.text: Then let's run it this Thursday at 02:30 UTC, when traffic is lowest.

later.speaker: Tom Becker
later.text: Works for me, I'll be up anyway.

streams.design: business; a one-off revenue item explained early makes the headline claim drafted later misleading

scene.scene: A startup's CEO and CFO prepare talking points for an investor update call that starts in an hour.

characters.name: Grace Kim
characters.background: will present on the investor call

primary_user.name: Grace Kim
primary_user.reason: she will say these talking points to investors

earlier.speaker: Grace Kim
earlier.text: Victor, give me the Q3 numbers before we write the talking points.

earlier.speaker: Victor Lin
earlier.text: Revenue was 3.4 million, up from 2.4 million in Q2.

earlier.speaker: Victor Lin
earlier.text: But 1.2 million of that is the one-time licensing deal with Helios. Subscription revenue alone was flat at about 2.2 million.

earlier.speaker: Grace Kim
earlier.text: Okay. And churn?

earlier.speaker: Victor Lin
earlier.text: Monthly churn ticked up to 3.1 percent, mostly small teams on the starter plan.

earlier.speaker: Grace Kim
earlier.text: Fine. Let me grab a coffee, then we write the script.

later.speaker: Grace Kim
later.text: Alright, opening: thank everyone for joining, then a quick recap of hiring.

later.speaker: Victor Lin
later.text: We closed four engineering hires this quarter and have two more offers out.

later.speaker: Grace Kim
later.text: Then the headline: revenue grew over forty percent quarter on quarter, and we expect that growth rate to continue into Q4.

later.speaker: Victor Lin
later.text: Sounds strong. Should we mention the new office too?
